#848. Nicole Taylor, Singer of Triplets Band Taylor Red, Dead at 35

Nicole Taylor—who formed the band Taylor Red with her identical twin sisters Nika Taylor and Natalie Taylor—has died at age 35: “We are shocked and heartbroken.”

Nicole Taylor, who was a member of the country music trio alongside triplet sisters Nika Taylor and Natalie Taylor, died on Sept. 28 following a battle with breast cancer, her siblings confirmed. She was 35.

“We are shocked and heartbroken to announce the passing of our sister Nicole Taylor. This isn’t the video we thought we’d ever be making,” Natalie said beside Nika in a video shared to YouTube Nov. 2. "We're still processing everything. This honestly feels really hard to talk about, but we're going to do our best in sharing some of her story.”

Though the sisters formed Taylor Red—formerly known as Red Roots—in 2011, they gained popularity in 2021 after their song “Country Money” went viral on social media.

But Natalie and Nika shared that one year later, Nicole had been diagnosed with "very aggressive" stage three breast cancer.

And while they’d hoped for a positive outcome following their sister’s 2022 diagnosis, Nika shared that they’ve found peace in knowing that their sister is “no longer suffering.”

“We thought she would be here sharing her story of earthly healing,” Nika explained, “but instead we’re here sharing her story of heavenly healing.”

Both Natalie and Nika recalled being with their older sister when she received her diagnosis.

"I just remember breaking down in absolute shock,” Natalie said. “I was just so surprised. We've been blessed with good health our whole life so this was a big shock and it wasn't what we were expecting.”

She continued, "I was crying and ran out to the hallway to tell Nika and I just remember Nicole said, 'God's going to use this for his glory.'"

Despite responding well to treatment and being told at one point she had "no evidence of the disease," Nicole's breast cancer returned and had progressed to stage four, which is when she was given just three months to live.

But Nicole beat those odds with “fearlessness,” living another year before she died last month. And in the face of tragedy, Natalie shared her faith has only strengthened since the loss.

“I've been a Christian a long time and something like this, you know, can make you either grow closer to God or distance yourself,” Natalie said. “This trial I would say grows that. I don’t know how someone could get through this kind of thing without God.”

The sisters confirmed on their website that the family held a private funeral service, adding that “Nicole, the oldest of us three sisters, will be greatly missed.”

“She was our leader and our best friend,” they added in the statement. “We are heartbroken, but we know she is in Heaven and will see her again.”

#846. Gilmore Girls' Milo Ventimiglia Gives Rare Nod to Ex Alexis Bledel

Gilmore Girls alum Milo Ventimiglia made a rare reference to his former girlfriend Alexis Bledel, whom he dated while filming the Amy Sherman-Palladino series.

Milo Ventimiglia has been out on the road for a long time.

But when he thinks back to his time on Gilmore Girls and his relationship with costar Alexis Bledel, he feels anything but lonely and so cold.

“What were those days like on set?” he reflected to Us Weekly in an interview published Nov. 2. “Hanging out with Jared Padalecki, being with Alexis—the experience is something that I always lean into, that really fills me up.”

The This Is Us star and Bledel’s onscreen chemistry as Jess and Rory found legs off camera, with the pair quietly dating for almost four years in the aughts before their 2006 breakup. But while their romance wasn’t destined to last, the pair’s relationship was and has always remained amicable.

In fact, some of the memories that stand out clearest for Ventimiglia—who shares two kids with wife Jarah Mariano—involve his former girlfriend.

“I remember shooting on the back lot of Warner Bros. with Alexis and getting on the bus and carrying a bag that the prop guy wanted to make really light,” he said. “But I [said], ‘Yeah, but it looks full and it’s huge, so it should be heavy. Put a sandbag in it.’ Those are the things that I think about.”

But while the Gilmore Girls fandom loves to examine the minutiae of every line, scene and episode—including the famously emphatic way Jesse asked Rory, “Why did you drop out of Yale?”—it’s the more general memories that fill him up like a cup of coffee.

“The episodes are for an audience to pick apart, dissect,” he added. “For us to make it, [it’s] the experience of making it.”

And loving it the way he do, Ventimiglia is ready to go to the ends of the earth to recall every beautiful moment for the upcoming HBO Max documentary about the Amy Sherman-Palladino show.

“I think the world of Amy, and Lauren [Graham],” he said, adding of the doc, “I have no idea what we’re going to talk about. It was 26 years ago that I made the show.”

He added, “It’s funny: I’ll have people run up to me and be like, ‘Hey, do you remember that time on Gilmore when you said this?’ I’m like, ‘That was 26 years ago.’ I’m like, ‘Tell me something about your life from 26 years ago.’ They’re like, ‘I wasn’t born.’”

But even more than a quarter century later, Jess and Rory remain a beloved onscreen pairing and a strong contender in the Gilmore Girls ship wars. For a look back at the show’s other onscreen couples in E!'s official ranking, read on.

He sued her father. He almost destroyed Luke and Lorelai's burgeoning relationship. He went by the nickname Digger. What more do we need to say?

They got married impulsively as teenagers (what a fun trope, said no one ever!) and then he promptly cheated on her. The only thing she got out of this marriage was disappointment and a mean meatloaf recipe.

We still can't believe a proposal with a thousand yellow daisies was wasted on a dud like Max Medin-ugh.

Remember that time Luke randomly married Nicole on a cruise ship? And then she cheated on him? Yeah, we try to forget about it, too.

Sorry, but the fact that he called her Mary (you know, Virgin Mary?) still creeps us out.

Rachel was Luke's first love, whose dreams were just too big for Stars Hollow. She was super-sweet and pushed Luke to realize his feelings for Lorelai. Thanks, girl!

OK, hear us out: Lane deserved more than Zack, who was a convenient filler for the void left by Adam Brody's exit. Sorry, not sorry. He's the rebound, NOT THE ONE.

Two weirdos, one weird relationship. Not the most epic of romances, but she did deal with his night terrors. So, true love.

Dave was definitely the one that got away (or, you know, ran off to become Seth Cohen on The O.C.). Come on, he inscribed his bible, with "This bible belongs to God but is being borrowed by Dave Rygalski." Swoon City, population: us.

You never forget your first love...but that doesn't mean you should continue an on-and-off relationship for over a decade. While we liked Christopher, we didn't love these two together, especially when they thought it was OK to run off and get married without Rory (their daughter!) being there. Unforgivable.

Fact: These two could take over and run their own country. They were made for each other.

Sigh, the unsung heroes of Stars Hollow also made up its most solid couple that flew so under the radar you often forgot about them...until you needed a cup of sugar from next door.

#845. China's influence in the gaming industry is growing

Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

In a dark underground hideout, dim light spills from a handful of oil lamps. A comrade fiddles with a rifle. A red flag hangs on one of the roughly hewn stone walls, bearing a hammer and sickle on a white star — the symbol of the ChineseWorkers' and Peasants' Red Army. Weapons are scattered on the ground. One is picked up, and soon the action moves into the snowy forest, where gunfire erupts among the trees.

Such a scene could fit in a new installment of "Call of Duty," the popular first-person shooter game that transports players to battlefields past, present, and future. But it is actually from "The Defiant." The game is currently being developed by the Chinese studio Hoothanes Technology in Hangzhou. It tells the story of Chinese forces fending off the Japanese army in the 1930s and 1940s.

Developer Connor Xu tells DW the weapons featured in the game are unique. They were used only in Asia and are therefore unfamiliar to many Western players, he says. The same goes for the story, which Xu says has never before been told in a video game.

"The Defiant" is also designed to appeal to an international audience. In just a few years, China has emerged as a major player in the global gaming industry despite strict regulations, censorship and a former ban on video game consoles.

More than 700 million people in China regularly play video games. According to market research company Newzoo, most consider gaming an important part of their lives. Many use games to stay in touch with friends.

"Games make life more interesting," developer Xu says. "I can try different roles, different stories, different characters, because we only have one life to live, but we can play a role in another story. That's really attractive, I think, to Chinese users."

People in China primarily play games on PCs and smartphones, while consoles are much less common. There are historical reasons for that: While gamers in Europe and North America debated whether PlayStation or Xbox was the better console in the early 2000s, the devices were not officially sold in China between 2000 and 2014. Chinese authorities said the restrictions were intended to protect children and teenagers from becoming addicted to gaming.

Minors in China are currently allowed to play online games for no more than three hours a week. There are no such limits for adults, but gaming is subject to strict controls. Anyone who wants to play must register using their real name and a personal identification number. That effectively allows the state to track who plays what and when, as well as whom they communicate with.

There is also a gray area that the Chinese government appears to tolerate. Some players log in using VPNs, giving them access to games that are not officially available in China. Some younger players use their parents' accounts to get around the limits on gaming time.

Despite its strict controls on underage gamers, China has become increasingly receptive to video games in general, having recognized the industry's enormous economic potential. Early on, games released for Chinese players often appeared to be copies of Western titles. At the same time, Chinese tech companies such as Tencent and NetEase invested in numerous Western gaming companies.

One distinctive feature of the Chinese market is its licensing system. "Unlike a lot of the other big video games markets in the world, China has a tightly regulated and licensed official video games market," George E. Osborn tells DW. The journalist advises NGOs and governments on video games and spoke at the Gamescom congress. In his book "Power Play," he describes how authoritarian states use video games to pursue political objectives.

The rule for all games in China is simple: No license, no sales. "That system essentially forces developers who want to release their video games to go through multiple layers of approval from China's Ministry of Propaganda, Ministry of Culture," Osborn says.

Games are prohibited from containing material that threatens China's unity, sovereignty or territorial integrity, among other restrictions. Pornographic content and gambling are also banned. Games may not incite crimes that threaten national security or spread information authorities believe could disrupt public order.

"The whole point around this criteria is that it's deliberately designed to be pretty vague," Osborn says. Whether a game violates the rules is a matter of interpretation. Sometimes games are altered even after release. In the 2025 action role-playing game "Wuchang: Fallen Feathers," for example, enemies based on famous Chinese figures from the Ming Dynasty suddenly could no longer be killed. Instead, they would collapse from exhaustion.

The Chinese action role-playing game "Black Myth: Wukong" became an unexpected international hit in 2024. By then, it was clear Chinese developers could do more than cater to the domestic market — they could create successful games for a global audience as well. The game was inspired by the 16th-century Chinese literary classic "Journey to the West."

Osborn sees nothing wrong with bringing Chinese culture to audiences around the world. The question, he says, is how much the state actually intervenes in the games themselves. "I think in general, video game players are actually quite deeply skeptical of these kinds of things. They are generally very good at spotting when someone might be selling to them or someone might be propagandizing. And so I think if it's too obvious, it won't work," he says.

Because of the licensing system, Western developers also have to comply with government requirements if they want to sell their games in China. And they do want to, Osborn says, because the market is too big to ignore. "But I think when you start thinking about the potential impact this has on creative standards around the world, I think it's really important that developers ask themselves the question of what will we or won't we compromise on here?"

He fears the real danger lies in self-censorship. That could lead developers, for example, to leave queer characters out of their games. That would represent a major step backward, he says, because games help many people explore their identities.

China is not the only country where games are modified to comply with national regulations. In Germany, for example, symbols that violate the country's constitution, such as the swastika, may not be shown in games unless the game in question explicitly contributes to the country's culture of remembrance. Depictions of extreme violence also have to be removed from German versions.

Glorifying violence is prohibited in China, too, yet Xu's team is still allowed to develop a war game. How does this add up? Xu explains it this way: "I think in this game, the most important thing is not violence. The most important thing is to tell history."

Xu says the team is committed to delivering a historically accurate product. Whether it succeeds will be for historians to judge.

This article was translated from German and edited by Sarah Hucal.

#844. ‘An absolute afterthought’: the story of the Nigeria women’s team’s fall from grace

The Super Falcons won’t be at the World Cup and with the prize money going up, they risk being left even further behind

It was a historic result in Casablanca – but not in a good way. Nigeria’s 2-1 defeat against South Africa in a playoff in August meant that the Super Falcons are missing out on the World Cup for the first time. It is a crushing blow for the most decorated national side in Africa across both men and women, one that has won no fewer than 10 Wafcon titles.

The journalist and lecturer Dr Victor Ademola was in Morocco the day of the defeat. “It was a very difficult evening,” he says. “Some players were visibly emotional while others appeared to be processing what had just happened. I saw players crying as they got on to the team bus while some sat alone or remained on their phones, looking very sad.”

The blow of missing out on the World Cup in Brazil next year came only a few days after they were eliminated from Wafcon at the quarter-final stage by Cameroon – only the semi-finalists qualified for the World Cup automatically, hence Nigeria ending up in that ill-fated playoff.

“What struck me most was the weight of what the result represented,” Ademola says. “These players knew the history of the Super Falcons and understood that this was not simply another defeat. There was a sense of disappointment, disbelief and heartbreak.”

The loss is not only historical but consequential. Nigeria will miss out on developmental funding with next year’s prize fund expected to rise from the previous tournament four years ago. In 2023 the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, pledged to equal the men’s and women’s tournaments prize funds by 2027. The figure for the men’s World Cup in the US, Canada and Mexico was $727m (roughly £539m). Recent news suggest Fifa will miss out on its target but it is nevertheless a blow for Nigeria not to be involved.

Janine Anthony, the African women’s football journalist, says the stakes for the Super Falcons were especially high as “women’s football does not have the luxury of not being at a World Cup”. Anthony adds: “A spot at the World Cup is the ultimate window and it’s a dream to be able to represent your country at any stage, whether it’s in music or football. For women’s football, the World Cup is such a commercially marketable vehicle. The Super Falcons team were one of only seven teams that had been to every World Cup, [and] the only African team. Now that’s gone.”

Anthony says that despite the Super Falcons’ success they are treated as an “absolute afterthought” in terms of the domestic leagues, management and preparation. The lack of preparation games proved problematic in Morocco, she suggests, manifesting itself in a lack of cohesiveness in most games. The then coach, Justine Madugu, frequently changed the starting XI throughout the tournament.

Before the tournament the team played two games against Senegal, who have never qualified for the World Cup, whereas before the 2025 edition they had three friendlies, against France, Cameroon and Portugal. “Imagine if they had more games to prepare,” Anthony says. “Then they could have probably done all the tweaking from a tactical perspective. The Nigerian Football Federation absolutely failed to capitalise on the Wafcon being moved to July.”

The landscape of African women’s football is changing, and Morocco are the only country from the continent who played in the 2023 World Cup who are guaranteed to be at next year’s tournament. South Africa are going into the inter-continental playoffs which start this month, and Nigeria and Zambia are out.

At the Wafcon, Malawi and Cameroon emerged as the standouts. It was Malawi’s debut at the tourmanent and the team gave a stellar performance with the attacking skill of the Chawinga sisters, Tabitha and Temwa, standing out. They will play at their first World Cup. The winners, Cameroon, were unexpected competitors at Wafcon, only qualifying after the Confederation of African Football expanded the tournament from 12 to 16 teams.

The Super Falcons’ absence from the World Cup next year is just the latest setback in a long line of disappointments. The men’s team have failed to qualify for two World Cups in a row while the under-17 men’s team have not reached the World Cup since 2019 or even Afcon since 2023. There have been signs of progress for the the under-20 women, who beat England 3-0 to reach the quarter-finals at their World Cup in September, but they then promptly lost against Colombia 1-0.

Players and coaches have long spoken out and protested against unpaid allowances and bonuses by the Nigerian Football Federation. The Super Falcons have staged numerous sit-ins and training boycotts to protest against the conditions, including at the Wafcons in 2004, 2016 and 2022 as well as the 2019 World Cup.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

The NFF is under investigation by the country’s department of state services for an alleged misuse of a 17bn naira (£9.5m) fund issued by the government in 2024 to address outstanding payments owed to players and staff of the national teams, according to local media. The NFF did not comment when contacted by the Guardian regarding the accusations.

Nigeria’s president, Bola Tinubu, is unhappy about the situation. “Nigerian football must undergo far-reaching changes to strengthen governance, administration, stakeholder representation, player development, domestic competitions and accountability,” he said in August.

That came shortly after Ibrahim Gusau resigned as NFF president along with several other board members. The NFF was scheduled to hold elections in September but they were suspended. They are now expected to take place following reforms made in consultation with Fifa and Caf.

What does the future hold for the Super Falcons? Anthony hopes for more investment, accountability and a bridge between veteran players and the current team on an administration level. “We can only hope that there is the understanding that the Nigerian fans are really disappointed and sad that their national teams aren’t bringing the joy that Nigerians are used to as a football loving nation,” she says. “We can only hope that the Super Falcons can finally be given the respect they’ve always deserved.”

#841. The Secrets Behind John Goodman's 200-Lb Weight Loss

After John Goodman hit his top weight of 400 pounds with years of yo-yo dieting, he was determined to get off the couch. Along with boxing, shared the actor, "It was basically just portion control."

While everyone loves a reboot, there's one character John Goodman hopes to never return to.

Ahead of the 2018 premiere of the Roseanne spinoff The Conners, the actor acknowledged that, yes, he had shed half of the weight from his formerly 400-pound frame, but he saw no point in talking it up.

"It was basically just portion control, and 'I don’t need it,'" The Righteous Gemstones star explained to AARP The Magazine in 2018 of cutting down on his food consumption. "I was just shoving everything into my mouth. But I don’t want to be an example to anybody when the weight comes thundering back on—when I start eating Crisco out of the can with a spoon and a side of confectioner's sugar."

Because he'd already had a taste of that yo-yo dieting.

"I'd lose 60 pounds in a summer, gain it all back. 70 pounds, 80 pounds," he recently shared with The New Yorker. "And that got tiring."

Having overcome a dependence on alcohol, he reasoned, "I was eating alcoholically after I stopped drinking."

So, he noted of undergoing a stomach operation, "I took steps so I wouldn’t have to do that anymore."

And nearly a decade later, he still remains righteous, most recently showing off his decidedly slimmer frame both on social media and at the September premiere of his and Tom Cruise's new film Digger.

But the process required the 74-year-old to, uh, dig deep.

When Roseanne's OG iteration went off the air in 1997—Goodman's Dan initially dying from a heart attack that was walked back for the reboot—"There was an emptiness inside me," the actor noted to AARP. "I still have it, but I know what it is now. You recognize it and go, 'There it is.' You don’t have to fill it with another pork chop or another drink."

He'd made the decision to get sober in 2007, following a three-decade battle with alcoholism—"It was 30 years of a disease that was taking its toll on everyone around me and it had got to the point where, every time I did it, it was becoming more and more debilitating. It was life or death," he expressed to The Guardian—yet he still felt hollow.

"But instead of filling it with booze or cocaine or food, you just acknowledge that it’s there," he explained to ABC's Peter Travers in 2016 of changing his eating habits. "You can’t fill it. And you go on and live with it."

Quite simply, he'd grown sick and tired of feeling sick and tired.

"You're shaving in the mirror and you don't want to look at yourself," he continued. "It gets dangerous."

Determined to ditch his couch potato nature—"It takes a lot of creative energy to sit on your ass and figure out what you're going to eat next," he reasoned to People in 2010—he hired health coach Mackie Shilstone to lead him through workouts six days a week and help him cut the sugar from his diet.

"I'm breaking a sweat," he acknowledged of his initial 100-pound weight loss, "but I'm not going nuts."

More importantly, he stopped running around in circles.

"In the old days, I would take three months out, lose 60 or 70 pounds," he recalled to ABC, "and then reward myself with a 6-pack of Bud or whatever and just go back to my old habits."

So, for this go-round, "I wanted to do it slowly, move, exercise," he continued. "I'm getting to the age where I can’t afford to sit still anymore. And it gives me the energy to work, 'cause work is very draining."

His new workouts packed quite the punch, though.

Sharing his boxing routine with Rolling Stone in 2023, Goodman said, "It's usually just an hour, hour and a half of hitting the mitts, hitting the bags, learning footwork. It's great."

And combined with a Mediterranean-style eating plan filled with fish, vegetables, olive oil and nuts, it proved to be a solid one-two.

But on days when Goodman wasn't feeling up for getting in the ring ("I never got good enough where I would trust myself to spar because once I get whacked in the face, I don't know if I wouldn't lose it," he told Rolling Stone), he didn't beat himself up.

Rather, he'd stay active by walking his dogs, hopping on an elliptical or sweating his way through other low-impact training.

Having fractured his hip in 2025 while filming Digger ("I was walking on set in my stocking feet, which was very stupid," he admitted to The New Yorker), he's focused on "building up the core, balance, strength training, stuff like that, so I don’t fall down."

And should he stumble, it takes just one glance in the mirror to remind himself how far he's come.

"I'm still trying to get used to my face," he acknowledged on the Nov. 2 episode of the Happy Sad Confused podcast. "It's weird. I think of myself as one way and then I look at myself, 'Oh, wow!'"

Though it's admittedly "strange," he added, "It's fun to get used to."

He joins a long list of stars who have had to adjust to a new normal. See what they've shared about their wellness journeys.

(Originally published Aug. 23, 2026, at 12 a.m. PT)

Tammy Slaton may be a star of TLC’s 1,000-Lb. Sisters, but she didn’t want to be beholden to that title forever.

“I’m down 500 pounds now, around 500,” the 38-year-old said in a confessional on an April 2025 episode of her show. “When I was at my heaviest, I was 700-plus pounds. Right now, I’m weighing in at 238.”

She underwent bariatric surgery in 2022, a choice her physician has praised as the right one for her.

“Tammy has consistently demonstrated her dedication to making sustainable lifestyle changes to maximize the benefits of her surgery,” Dr. Eric Smith told People in October 2024. “I've emphasized the importance of making small, daily adjustments to ensure not only her continued progress but also her long-term success. She's truly committed to her health journey.”

It seems as if every time Jelly Roll hits a red carpet, he’s down a sizable slice of weight.

“I started at 540 pounds and I was 357 pounds this morning,” the singer born Jason DeFord told Pat McAfee in April 2025 during the ESPN host's Big Night Aht live show. “I’m gonna lose another 100 pounds and go skydiving with my wife in Sweden, baby!"

The 6-foot-1 artist admittedly needed to overhaul his relationship with food to get where he wanted to go. "I've always said that I believe obesity is directly connected to mental health," he explained on an October 2024 episode of On Purpose With Jay Shetty. "I know how easy it is for people to go, 'Just quit eatin' so much, just work out, it's so easy!' I wish I looked at food that way.”

Weight was still “the mountain” in front of him, Jelly Roll noted, but his lifestyle changes were working.

"I'm learning, I'm being very diligent with it,” he said. “I'm taking it serious, I'm drinking a bunch of water, I'm cold plunging, I'm eating right, I'm doing good."

The Mean Girls alum shared he dropped over 100 pounds amid a three-year health journey.

"Three years, Franzese wrote in a post on Threads in September 2026. "Down 135lbs No booze, No sugar, workout 4 times a week (or more) now counting macros."

The Fresh Off the Boat alum used to weigh 300 pounds and lost 130, showcasing his journey on TikTok.

Al Roker wasn’t kidding around with the title of his cookbook Recipes to Live By.

Because having lost a hard-fought 100 pounds, the longtime TODAY weatherman literally walks the walk (aiming for at least 10,000 steps a day), watching what he eats and fitting in some sort of exercise on a daily basis.

“My mantra is ‘something is better than nothing,’” he told People in a June 2025 interview. “Maybe you’ll be running marathons or entering weight-lifting contests, but I think most people just want a level of fitness that improves their quality of life.”

Roker underwent gastric bypass surgery in 2002 to get his fitness journey underway, but, he acknowledged, “There’s no magic bullet.”

Surgery is “not the end,” he advised. “You’re still going to have to put in the work.”

While previously known for the tush push, former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce has been busy showing off his buff bod.

Not that the athlete wasn’t in fighting shape during his 13-year career in the NFL, but he’s down at least 25 pounds from his playing weight of 295, sharing during the 2025 Truist Championship pro-am golf tournament in Philly that he weighed around 270.

All of which is part of his retirement plan. “I feel like for some reason, 250 to 260 feels like I'll be still big and be happy with the way I look without having a six-pack,” Kelce told GQ in June 2024. “But I’ll still be able to have that stature a little bit.”

Really, the most important aspect for the father of four daughters with wife Kylie Kelce was to be able to keep pace with his kids.

Then weighing in at 277, “my back already feels better,” he shared. “My knees already feel better. So another 20 pounds hopefully will make that much more adept at playing with my children.”

It wasn’t just a change of scenery that did the trick for Rosie O’Donnell, who relocated with her family from the U.S. to Ireland.

"I've lost more weight here,” she shared in a March 2025 TikTok. “I am on Mounjaro for my diabetes and one of the side effects is you lose weight.”

The former View cohost had recently gone shopping for better-fitting clothes in Dublin. “I’m one of those people,” she said, “who's always had a weight issue and now that I'm a size large, instead of an XL or a 2XL, I find it shocking.”

Jazz Jennings embarked on a diet-and-fitness journey in 2022, explaining on Instagram two years later, “I finally care about myself after years of neglecting my health. I had truly let myself go when it came to eating. I am so proud of my weight loss, and I feel my confidence radiates through."

In August 2024, the I Am Jazz star shared that she had lost almost 100 pounds and was “so proud” of her progress.

It turns out Christopher Schwarzenegger is a chip off the ol’ muscly block.

The youngest of Arnold Schwarzenegger and ex-wife Maria Shriver’s four kids together laid low while he dropped 30 pounds, but now he’s back in action.

“It’s not an overnight thing, but it took a lot of trial and error,” he shared in May 2025 at the Inaugural Beacher Vitality Happy & Healthy Summit, noting that just giving up bread made a big difference. “And even still to this day, when [I look at] before and after photos, I don’t feel like I’m an ‘after’ yet.”

Meanwhile, Christopher did not let a certain seven-time Mr. Olympia in on his plan.

“I could never go and say to him, 'You’re overweight,'” dad Arnold told The Times in June 2025. "We just kept introducing healthy foods. We introduced him always to the gym and all of that kind of stuff. And then, out of nowhere, he decided that he wanted to be lean. And now he is. So that is of course fantastic, the self-discipline and the self-motivation. I always felt one day it will have to come from him—and it did.”

Chrissy Metz doesn’t like to run “unless I’m being chased,” she quipped, but she’s a big fan of strength training—and working out is part of the regimen that resulted in her losing 100 pounds.

“I want to age the best way that I can, and I want to be strong,” the This Is Us alum told DailyMail.com in April 2025. “And that’s really the impetus behind any of it.”

To Metz, aging gracefully means “staying strong and flexible,” so she tries to be active every day.

Being a big teddy bear of a guy was part of the package when John Goodman starred on Roseanne in the 1990s, at one point “pushing 400” pounds, as he told David Letterman in 2010. By the time The Conners premiered in 2018, however, family patriarch Dan Conner had made a few lifestyle adjustments.

Goodman quit drinking in 2007, the first step on his road to getting in better shape, while his favorite activities included boxing and walking his dogs.

“I’m breaking a sweat but I’m not going nuts,” he told People in 2010, sharing he had lost about 100 pounds working out six days a week and cutting sugar out of his diet.

Overall, the 6-foot-2 actor has lost about 200 pounds since he was at his peak weight.

“I just got tired, sick and tired of looking at myself,” Goodman told ABC News in 2016. “You’re shaving in the mirror and you don’t want to look at yourself. It gets dangerous.”

Oprah Winfrey has been sharing the highs and lows of her weight loss journey for decades.

From donning skinny jeans and rolling out a wagon loaded with 67 pounds of fat to wow her Oprah Winfrey Show audience in 1988, to buying a stake in WeightWatchers in 2015, she has used her platform to keep the conversation going.

And taking on the topic du jour, she revealed in March 2024 on An Oprah Special: Shame, Blame and the Weight Loss Revolution that, along with eating smaller portions and staying active, she was taking medication to help regulate her weight.

"It's not just one thing,” she said of her secret to staying fit, “it's multiple things.”

Her goal with the special, Winfrey explained, was to “start releasing the stigma and the shame and the judgment—to stop shaming other people for being overweight or how they choose to lose or not lose weight—and more importantly to stop shaming ourselves."

Lizzo simply wanted to feel better from head to toe.

“Once I started working out for mental health, to have balanced mental health or endorphins, so that I don't look at myself in the mirror and feel ashamed of myself, and feel disgusted with myself,” the “Good as Hell” singer explained in a May 2023 TikTok, “exercise has helped me shift my mind, not my body.”

She acknowledged in a January 2025 TikTok that she was on an “intentional weight loss journey,” her goal was simply to be the best version of herself.

“Even at the end of my weight loss journey, I'm not going to be considered thin by any means,” Lizzo said. “I will still be considered morbidly obese on the BMI and little bros on the internet are still going to call me 'big backed.' But I will be happy."

A second later, the video jumped to Lizzo exclaiming, “And I am happy,” as she showed off a screen showing her body fat had gone down by 16 percent and she’d shaved 10.5 points from her Body Mass Index (BMI).

“Let this be a reminder that you can do anything—anything—you set your mind to,” she added. “Now I guess it’s time to set new goals.”

#840. Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?

Would you work 12 hours straight? The CDU/CSU and SPD are locked in a dispute over reforms to the Working Hours Act. Workplace flexibility, collective bargaining agreements and worker protection rules are at stake.

The town of Leuna, in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt, is one of the country's largest chemical industry hub, where more than 100 companies have established operations. Among them is the Finnish biotechnology group UPM, which has recently built a biorefinery for wood-based chemicals in Leuna. It's now hiring.

One of the job listings is for a chemical technician to oversee the rollout of new facilities. But to qualify, candidates must be willing to work 12-hour shifts. Is that legal? According to German law, standard working hours are limited to eight hours per day. It is permissible to extend this to ten hours, provided that workers receive compensatory time off for the overtime, and there must be at least 11 hours of rest between two shifts.

Business associations and the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties have long called for these rules to be made more flexible.

Rainer Dulger, president of the Confederation of German Employers' Associations (BDA), points to the European Working Time Directive, which allows for a maximum weekly working time of 48 hours. "The allowance is being taken advantage of almost everywhere else — except here," Dulger told the dpa news agency in August.

Companies say they often find the existing rules too rigid, particularly in industries with seasonal fluctuations — such as tourism — or in project-based work, or during irregular peaks in workload, such as in the restaurant industry. They could deploy their staff more efficiently, says Dulger: "The Working Hours Act dates back to the era of fax machines and rotary-dial phones. It knows nothing of laptops or daycare hours."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In their 2025 coalition agreement, the CDU/CSU and the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) agreed to reform the Working Hours Act. "In keeping with the European Working Time Directive, we want to allow for a maximum weekly rather than daily working time — also and especially to promote a better work-life balance," the agreement said.

The SPD would have preferred to leave the law unchanged, but had to accept the conservative parties' plans. The Social Democrats pointed out that longer working hours are already permitted in exceptional cases, such as in emergency services, the health care sector and security services. Workers in power plants, refineries and the chemical industry are also allowed to work up to 12 hours at a time.

Even Chancellor Friedrich Merz himself seemed unaware of this exception until quite recently. After visiting the UPM refinery in Leuna in September, he recounted to business leaders at the German Employers' Day in Berlin that he was "completely surprised" to learn that the facilities operate on a continuous 12-hour shift schedule, thanks to the approval of the works council.

Merz recounted the shift supervisor describing the work schedule as "really great" — with three-day work weeks. "He said we have plenty of time for our families — it's a great way to organize things." Merz went on to conclude that this demonstrates the benefits of relaxing the Working Hours Act.

"Working more than eight hours is not exploitation. Rather, it can be a good opportunity to organize working hours more flexibly — both for businesses and for the people working there," the chancellor said. "We should do it."

But there is resistance from within the SPD and from trade unions opposed to amending the Working Hours Act. The trade union Verdi argues that significantly longer workdays would have negative consequences for employees' health and would disadvantage people with family and caregiving responsibilities. In certain industries, employees could also be put under pressure to accept longer shifts.

An initial reform draft was drawn up in June 2026 by the Labor and Social Affairs Ministry, headed at the time by Bärbel Bas, an SPD politician who has since resigned for personal reasons.

The draft includes some conditions, including a collective bargaining agreement between employers and unions if any schedule changes were made, as well as health and safety regulations, and working hours to be tracked electronically.

Annika Klose, spokesperson for labor and social policy for the SPD parliamentary group, explained the thinking behind the idea. Flexibility, she said, is "not a one-way street." The coalition agreement explicitly aims to promote a better balance between family and work. "So that it's sometimes possible to take your child to football practice in the afternoon and then continue working afterward — but not that my boss tells me against my will: 'You're working the shift from 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. tomorrow.'"

The CDU/CSU immediately rejected the draft. Businesses were also up in arms. "This draft must be withdrawn and completely revised," demanded Dulger in a statement, saying it was "steeped in mistrust." The German Confederation of Skilled Crafts (ZDH) spoke of a "breach of the commitments agreed to in the coalition agreement." The reform has been on hold ever since.

At the Employers' Day event, Merz held out the prospect of progress. "This is indeed long overdue. I believe we can accomplish this relatively quickly and create flexibility in the labor market."

It remains to be seen, however, whether the new SPD Labor Minister, Alexander Schweitzer, shares this view. In early October, his party released a paper on reforming working hours that read like a declaration of war against the CDU. "Self-determination, Not Deregulation" is the title of the seven-page document that was signed by the SPD working group on labor, the youth organization Jusos, the "60plus" working group and the women's wing of the SPD.

In the paper, the Social Democrats not only reiterate the points that already appeared in Bas' draft back in June. They also demand that, in the future, employers and employees should decide on working hours "jointly and by mutual agreement." They argued that it is not "in the spirit of a modern reform of working time law" if only employers can determine when employees finish work.

From a political perspective, the dispute over reforming work hours has long become more than just a debate over legal provisions. It is a fundamental dispute over how much flexibility workers should be expected to tolerate in the future and to what extent the state should protect them. And it is yet another stumbling block for the already beleaguered government in Berlin.

#839. Green backs 'proven' Parker for Hammers job

Scott Parker has faced his old club West Ham four times as a manager, losing three and drawing one

Former West Ham United goalkeeper Rob Green says Scott Parker's "proven record" of getting teams promoted from the Championship would make him the perfect fit as the club's next manager.

Parker, 46, is expected to replace Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday following West Ham's disappointing start to the season after relegation.

A three-time former club player of the year at West Ham, Parker has led Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion as a manager.

"Scott's shown a proven record of getting promoted," Green, a former team-mate of Parker's, told BBC Radio London.

"Detractors of Scott would say, 'this is not a really imaginative style of play, it's not one that might thrill the fans'. I think Scott would say, 'well, actually, my team knows exactly what it needs to do to get promoted'.

"There's so much quality in that side that they should still get promoted. You get in the Premier League, you stay in the Premier League, then you worry about the style of football.

"Give the stardust in that [West Ham] front line to him [and] he can give you a really good platform to go forwards with it. It makes perfect sense to me."

Green: 'Scott's teams know how to get up.'

Widely seen as favourites for automatic promotion after dropping out of the Premier League last season, West Ham are currently eighth in the Championship, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough.

They have won two of their last six games and have lost back-to-back home matches - going down 3-2 to Southampton and then 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.

The decision to sack Nuno means West Ham are looking for their fourth permanent manager since David Moyes left the London Stadium in May 2024.

Another former West Ham player, John Moncur, said the club were too hasty in letting Moyes go, but also backed Parker for the job.

"I don't think we would have been in this position if Moyes had stayed, because he's that type of manager that wouldn't have allowed the things to happen that did," Moncur told BBC Radio London.

"[Scott] has done a good job at other clubs, he knows the club backwards and it seems to fit.

"They are a very educated bunch of fans, you can't pull the wool over their eyes. Scott will know that.

"It's getting the balance right. It's no good playing lovely football if you're not winning matches."

Moncur: 'You don't want to become adrift.'

#837. Chinese doctoral students in clinical medicine can graduate without a thesis — more degrees to follow

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Postgraduate students studying clinical medicine in China have the option to graduate with a practical achievement, such as an analysis of a special clinical case, rather than a thesis.Credit: Xie Shangguo/VCG via Getty

Master’s and doctoral candidates in some clinical medicine degrees in China can now graduate with a ‘practical achievement’ instead of a thesis. This is the second field to open such a pathway. Since 2024, master’s and PhD students in engineering have been allowed to graduate from universities across China after developing a new product, technique, project or installation.

On 22 October, a team of government-appointed education advisers released draft policy documents setting out the rules for the graduation pathway for students pursuing a professional master’s or doctoral degree in clinical medicine — both are three-year courses typically taken by medical graduates and practising physicians.

In China, professional postgraduate courses focus on training students to solve problems in a particular line of work rather than developing research skills, as they would in an academic degree. The rules state that students have the option to graduate with a practical achievement, such as an analysis of a special clinical case or an investigation into a problem facing medical institutes.

Postgraduate courses in translation, agriculture, accounting and arts are expected to introduce similar pathways to graduation, according to China’s Academic Degrees Committee of the State Council, a government body driving reforms for postgraduate education.

These reforms are a step in the right direction, because students preparing for professional careers should be trained and assessed in ways that reflect those careers, says Futao Huang, a researcher of higher-education policy at Hiroshima University in Higashihiroshima, Japan. “The real challenge is to develop credible, transparent and profession-specific standards for assessing practical achievements,” Huang adds.

For students pursuing a professional degree in clinical medicine, the new graduation pathway means that they can be assessed on the contribution that their research will bring to patients and society, says Zhou Feifei, a spinal surgeon at Peking University Third Hospital in Beijing. “This will encourage them to find problems in real life and to address the problem using a scientific way,” he adds.

One of Zhou’s students, Tie Dazhao, was the first person to graduate with a ‘practical PhD’ in clinical medicine in June, having been selected as a pilot case in 2023. Tie developed an artificial-intelligence-empowered software programme that can help physicians to classify a type of rare spinal condition and recommend suitable treatment strategies to them, says Zhou.

Individual universities are encouraged to form their own policies on training practical postgraduate students and what requirements students must meet to graduate, says Liping Duan, chief physician of gastroenterology at Peking University Third Hospital and a member of a national advisory committee tasked with formulating the policy for clinical medicine. One of the biggest challenges will be creating a uniform standard to assess practical achievements, Duan says. “What works for cardiology may not work for dermatology, for example,” she adds.

How to control the quality of the achievements will also be important, Duan says. “Some people may mistakenly think that graduation has become easier now that students can choose not to write a thesis.”

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03480-7

Correction 03 November 2026: A previous version of this story used PhD students instead of doctoral students.

#836. Football Daily | West Ham want promotion – so it’s time to call in an understated club legend

Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!

While Football Daily hasn’t actually seen much of West Ham this season, we’ve noted enough of their results to presume they were doing OK in their attempt to bounce back to the Premier League after relegation. Less than a third of the way through the Championship season under Nuno Espírito Santo, they’d already spanked six without reply past both Wrexham and Lincoln, while scoring three or more in wins over Wolves, Derby and Bolton. However, it turns out that of the 13 matches they’ve played in a league that is famously difficult to get out of (unless you were Sheffield Wednesday last season), they have actually lost three times and currently sit in eighth place, a whopping six points off leaders Middlesbrough. Given the context of such an unbridgeable chasm, it is small wonder West Ham fans woke up to news that Nuno had been unceremoniously bounced out of the London Stadium with a P45 in hand.

Coming on the back of consecutive home defeats by Southampton and West Brom, Tuesday’s news won’t have come as a huge surprise to Hammers fans, treated to the sight of a sad Nuno on the London Stadium touchline on Saturday, eyes glazed and grey beard glistening in the early evening mist as he stared blankly in the direction of several celebrating Baggies. “West Ham United can confirm that men’s first-team head coach Nuno Espírito Santo has left his position with immediate effect,” droned a club statement. “Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club’s objectives and expectations remain on track.”

Determined to secure one of the two automatic promotion places up for grabs, West Ham have decided to nip any prospective long-term slump in the bud by approaching Scott Parker. An understated club legend of sorts, the 46-year-old is best known for wearing expensive Thom Browne four-bar ripstop blouson jackets in his technical area while masterminding immediate promotion to the Premier League for the only three English clubs he has managed thus far.

Indeed, it is a testament to the breezy optimism of certain West Ham fans on several Social Media Disgraces that they are already discussing how dismal Parker’s Premier League record is, while arguing over who should replace him when he becomes the first top-flight gaffer to get sacked in 12 months’ time. With their team having scored 33 goals in their opening 13 games this season, West Ham fans can now presumably look forward to seeing them bag the same number in their remaining fixtures as they clock up 33 consecutive, risk-averse 1-0 wins. It may not be the fabled West Ham way but it will do until the next guy comes along.

#832. Andoni Iraola calls on Liverpool to sharpen up in attack before Fenerbahce test

Reds target fourth straight Champions League win

Turkish side led by ex-Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt

Andoni Iraola has said Liverpool must improve their attacking play but dismissed concerns over the contrast between his team’s output in the Premier League and Champions League.

Liverpool boast a 100% record in Europe this season and can take a significant step towards qualification for the knockout phase with victory away at Fenerbahce on Wednesday. Former Liverpool favourite Dirk Kuyt will take charge of his first European game with the Turkish club, having replaced Ismail Kartal on an interim basis last week.

Iraola’s side failed to register a shot on target, according to Opta, during Sunday’s defeat by Arsenal, the first time Liverpool have drawn a blank in a Premier League home game since Opta records began in 2003-04. The Liverpool head coach believes the statistic did not reflect his team’s performance but admitted there is room for improvement.

“It is difficult when you lose but honestly I am happy with a lot of things from the other day,” said Iraola, who is without the injured Ryan Gravenberch in Istanbul. “But we still need to improve, especially attacking the box. A lot of times we were there with the numbers but we were not making the proper runs and waiting for second balls. We put Arsenal under pressure and they defended well but I liked a lot of things.”

Liverpool have scored more goals in three Champions League games this season (12) than in nine Premier League fixtures (11) but Iraola denied the disparity is a serious concern.

He added: “We have had better results in the Champions League and Carabao Cup than the Premier League but it’s very early in the season for these comparisons. We want to continue this run in the Champions League. This is a good chance to get to 12 points and try to qualify, and then try to finish in the top eight, but Champions League away games are difficult, especially in this stadium and this atmosphere. We have to be mentally very ready.”

Kuyt returned to Fenerbahce as Kartal’s assistant only this summer – he played for the club for three seasons after leaving Liverpool in 2012 – but was appointed interim coach following Kartal’s resignation in the wake of last week’s 2-1 defeat by Galatasaray.

The former Liverpool striker said: “Tomorrow will be a very special occasion for me but, at the stage we are in, I’m not the important person. It’s about the club. Romelu [Lukaku] was speaking about how important it is to show the fans – who deserve much more – a reaction and a good performance. We have really good players but we need to show up. Liverpool are an amazing team but so are Fenerbahce. If the fans show up, I think Europe will see how big this fanbase is.”

Iraola, meanwhile, said he has not received or sought an explanation from Pro Ref over the decision not to award Liverpool a penalty for Jurriën Timber’s shirt-pull on Alexander Isak on Sunday.

He said: “I didn’t ask for an explanation and I haven’t received an explanation, no. I told you what I thought about the penalties at the time but, honestly, I don’t have the time [to ask Pro Ref]. There is just two days between games and I have been preparing for Fenerbahce.”

#831. Soccer Player Jesús de Miguel Dead at 30 After Collision on Field

CD Tenerife’s center striker Jesús de Miguel died at the age of 30 following a midgame collision with FC Andorra’s goalkeeper, during which he was struck in the chest.

The soccer world is reeling after a devastating accident.

Spain’s Jesús de Miguel, who was a center striker for CD Tenerife, died at the age of 30 after being struck in the chest during the team’s match against FC Andorra on Nov. 2.

“Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats, and unable to believe this is true,” de Miguel’s team shared on their official website Nov. 3, translated from Spanish, “CD Tenerife announces the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda.”

The statement continued, “There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow. We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire Tenerife community, who today mourn this cruel outcome.”

The accident occurred during the last few seconds of the Spanish second division match. While chasing the ball near the field’s halfway line, de Miguel collided with Andorra’s goalkeeper Jesús Owono.

As Owono tried to clear the ball at speed, the goalkeeper—who had moved far out from the goal—accidentally struck de Miguel in the chest with his knee.

The move earned him an immediate red card and he was ejected from the game, however, Owono made his way back onto the pitch after the severity of de Miguel’s injuries became clear.

The striker had gone down clutching his chest before lying motionless on the pitch. While medical staff treated de Miguel for more than minutes on the field, per Reuters, he was eventually rushed to a local hospital for additional treatment where he later passed away.

According to local Spanish outlets, the National Police have opened an investigation into the incident, with the High Court of Justice of the Canary Islands telling outlet El País that such procedure is standard for any death without natural cause.

Following de Miguel’s death, FC Andorra shared a statement expressing their grief. (As of the morning of Nov. 3, per CNN, Owono had deactivated his Instagram account.)

“Devastated and with broken hearts,” the team wrote on social media, “we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace.”

Meanwhile, the president of CD Tenerife Felipe Miñambres detailed the organization’s devastation.

“We are all going through very difficult moments now, of sadness and of not believing what happened,” he told Reuters. “But we’ll go through the mourning all together, and we’ll be with all the people going through this feeling that should make us be more together.”

#830. Arteta backs Saliba’s readiness to return for Arsenal at Slavia Prague

Defender travelled with squad after long injury absence

‘I have clips’: Arteta hits back after Liverpool complaints

Mikel Arteta is confident that William Saliba is ready to make his first appearance of the season for Arsenal after he played 45 minutes of a match behind closed doors last week.

The France defender started training on his own last month after the back injury he sustained at the World Cup but has since resumed full training and on Tuesday travelled with Arsenal’s squad to face Slavia Prague. It remains to be seen whether Saliba will feature in the Czech capital given such a lengthy absence, although Arteta insisted that he has no doubts the 25-year-old is primed to return.

Asked whether he would treat his comeback with caution, the Arsenal manager said: “Yes, but now you are in, or not. And now he’s in, and he’s in like anybody else. All the preparation has been done to measure all the loads and all the steps that he had to do to minimise that risk.

“Now he’s in a really good place. He’s built the capacity that we needed, and now it’s about giving him minutes. He’s a centre-back, and when that’s the case, it’s not like an attacking midfielder or a nine that you can change. A centre-back normally has to be able to play 90 minutes, and that’s why all the preparation that we’ve done to build him.”

Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães were outstanding in Arsenal’s landmark victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday and Arteta admitted that Saliba’s return is likely to give him a selection headache. Konsa is also capable of playing at right-back, although he will face competition from Ben White and Jurriën Timber.

The latter escaped punishment against Liverpool when he pulled Alexander Isak’s shirt inside the penalty area and Arteta hit back at suggestions that officials could try to balance out that decision in future.

“I have a lot of clips about shirts, pulls, grabs. So I have a massive library that we can talk about,” Arteta said in an echo of his comments last month about straying outside his technical area. “We’re talking about one in particular. I have a massive library that we can throw there to remind everybody what every team is going through.”

Max Dowman is also in contention to play against Slavia as he serves a three-match domestic suspension for his red card against Fleetwood last week. He became the first 15-year-old to feature in the Champions League against the same opponents 12 months ago and could break Cesc Fàbregas’s record as the youngest Arsenal player to start in the competition.

“That’s a chapter that is gone. It’s a moment of learning from all of us, and we move on,” Arteta said of Dowman’s dismissal against Fleetwood. “He’s been engaged. Today we spent some time together, talking about things in training. He’s always super positive. When you’re 16 you have a different way of looking at things and treating things, and that’s what he brings to the team as well.”

#829. How Hoda Kotb and Joel Schiffman Remain Friendly Exes

While Hoda Kotb ended her engagement with financier Joel Schiffman in 2022, the Today alum knows her ex is a good egg. And when it comes to parenting their daughters, they've found the right recipe.

For Hoda Kotb, the true trick to getting through the tougher parts of parenting is remembering what a treat it all is.

Take the time the former Today Show anchor was attempting to feed then-infant Haley while letting pup Blake outside only to have her dog shatter a picture frame. "She's crying," she recounted to Us Weekly in 2018, "he's barking, there's poop on the floor, glass is broken. I was like, 'I might have a breakdown.' Then I remember thinking, 'I would have begged God for this.'"

And for the most part, motherhood truly is everything it's cracked up to be—even when it involves co-parenting with your former fiancé.

Thankfully, financier Joel Schiffman is a good egg, gamely cracking up with Kotb in their matching deviled egg costumes on Halloween.

Not that the two have had to, er, walk on eggshells since their 2022 split.

"Joel is one of the best people I know, and he really is a great human being," Kotb explained on The Jamie Kern Lima Show in 2024. "And I feel like I'm a pretty great human being, but sometimes two great human beings together isn't quite enough to make it work."

But when it comes to parenting Haley, now 9, and her younger sister Hope, 7, the once-betrothed pair are star students.

Before whipping up their joint Halloween costumes, the exes reunited for their daughters' first day of school in September, Christmas morning and regular family dinners.

Because while the duo never made it down the aisle following their 2019 engagement, she remains committed to doing life with the 68-year-old.

"I went to this retreat and had kind of an epiphany about my life and I was realizing that you can love someone—like I loved him very much, and still do to this day—but that person isn't right for you in that moment," Kotb explained during a 2025 appearance on Today, months after she signed off from her 16-year hosting role.  "And you can say to yourself, 'Wow, I'm ready to try to get other buckets of mine filled.'"

These days she's simply brimming with gratitude.

She credits her former partner with giving her the confidence to pursue adoption in the first place, telling People in 2022, "it's because of Joel that I have Haley and Hope, without question. I think I might have been too afraid to do it alone."

And though they've ended their romantic relationship, the two remain co-hosts when it comes to creating a magical childhood for their girls.

Having traded her Today gig for a new role helming her wellness brand and media company Joy 101, "Now I can feel my life slowing down a little, like I feel more of a rhythm," the 62-year-old explained on the morning show in 2025. "I have barbecues in the backyard, and Joel comes. We invite neighbors over. We have kids running around. There’s a dog."

#827. Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision

Police homicide division opens judicial proceedings

He was struck in the chest when challenging for ball

Spanish football was in shock on Tuesday after the Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a match in the second division. The homicide division of the national police has opened judicial proceedings into a possible involuntary manslaughter, a routine procedure after any death not by natural causes. The chief public prosecutor in Santa Cruz de Tenerife told the state news agency EFE that it was “very difficult” for a case to come to court.

Tenerife announced that De Miguel had died at 8am on Tuesday after he had been taken into intensive care on Monday afternoon. He did not regain consciousness after a cardiorespiratory arrest.

The collision occurred in added time at the end of Andorra’s visit to Tenerife, a game put back 24 hours because of the risk of torrential rain. With the score 2-2, in the 96th minute, a long ball was played away from the Tenerife area and up the pitch. De Miguel chased it into space and Owono came a long way out of his goal, jumping forward, with his right knee up, and crashing into the attacking player inside the centre circle.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

Owono was sent off, walking straight to the touchline. De Miguel was left unconscious, with players from both sides appealing for medical assistance. The match was abandoned by the referee, Manuel Ángel Pérez Hernández, having run into the 108th minute.

Medics restored De Miguel’s pulse in the ambulance and transferred him to the Hospital Universitario de Nuestra Señora de Candelaria in Santa Cruz. Tenerife said he was able to breathe unassisted and was stable but that he remained unconscious and in a critical condition. At 5am the club announced De Miguel’s condition had worsened neurologically.

“CD Tenerife announce the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda on Tuesday 3 November 2026 at 8:00am,” said a statement released at 9.31am. The statement described the club as “broken by pain, with a lump in the throat and unable to believe that this is true”, and accompanying the forward’s “devastated family, loved ones and everyone associated with Tenerife who mourns this cruel end … there are no words of consolation”.

The former Barcelona defender Gerard Piqué, who is Andorra’s majority shareholder and attended the game, wrote on social media: “I am so deeply sorry, to my soul. Rest in peace, Jesús.” The club’s president, Ferran Vilaseca, told reporters: “This has had a huge emotional impact on our players, coaching staff and everyone at FC Andorra. Our sincerest condolence arriving on the Spanish mainland after midnight, still unaware of the outcome.”

The chief public prosecutor in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, José Luis Sánchez-Jáuregui, told EFE it was “very difficult” for a legal case to be taken up given that the impact happened in the course of the game. A formal legal complaint could still be brought. Sentences for involuntary homicide range from three months to four years of imprisonment. There is no precedent of a footballer facing legal proceedings as a result of a challenge in the course of a game.

According to federation protocols Owono could face a 12-game ban, with the disciplinary committee due to decide.

The report from the referee said: “In minute 90+6, player no 25 Ferrer Owono, Jesus Lazaro, was sent off for the following reason: for impacting sharply upon an opponent with his leg high and excessive force in dispute of the ball. The player was treated on the field of play, which he then abandoned on a stretcher. At the close of this report, no medical certificate had been presented.”

Tenerife have asked to postpone their next two games, against Granada on Saturday and Badajoz in the cup the following week. Andorra have requested that their meeting with Mallorca at the weekend be postponed. The Spanish football federation announced the postponement of all games due to be held on Tuesday in the Copa del Rey and the Copa de la Reina.

Clubs across Europe, including Barcelona and Real Madrid, paid tribute to De Miguel. “Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times,” Barcelona said. Real Madrid said they sent “condolences and affection to his family, his teammates, his club, and all his loved ones”.

De Miguel had played most of his career in Spain’s third tier, at Leganés B, Inter Madrid, Fuenlabrada, Navalcarnero, Unionistas de Salamanca and Castellón. He was Castellón’s top scorer when they were promoted to the second division in 2024 and joined Tenerife in 2025.

#826. Championship roundup: Devlin’s double for Portsmouth denies Swansea top spot

Birmingham sink Millwall to keep up good form

Norwich thump Rams and pile pressure on Eustace

Terry Devlin’s double denied Swansea the chance to take top spot in the Championship as in-form Portsmouth won 3-1 at Fratton Park.

Devlin’s first-half goal looked like it was going to be enough for Pompey but Zan Vipotnik, the Championship’s top scorer last season, won and converted an 85th-minute penalty to set up a blockbuster finale.

Devlin’s smart finish from a corner in the second minute of stoppage time and Tommy Waddingham’s strike six minutes later made sure Pompey made it six without defeat, and Middlesbrough – who play on Wednesday – remained at the summit.

Alex Cochrane scored inside a minute as Birmingham buried Millwall with a first-half goal rush to earn a 3-0 win at St Andrew’s.

Cochrane, Max Bird and Jay Stansfield scored with left-footed finishes before half-time to ease the loss of seven-goal striker August Priske with a knee problem. It put City on their way to their sixth win in eight and extended their unbeaten Championship home start to seven games.

Samuel Edozie’s second-half equaliser ensured Southampton and West Brom shared the points from a 1-1 draw at the Hawthorns. Both teams started the season in promising fashion and taking a point apiece means the sides continue their respective unbeaten runs after a game of two halves.

West Brom completely dominated the first half as Southampton failed to register a single shot in the opening 45 and Isaac Price scored from the penalty spot to give the hosts a deserved half-time lead for his fifth goal of the season.

For all the hosts’ dominance, Tonda Eckert’s side turned the tables in the second period and found an equaliser through Edozie. Both teams missed chances to take three points in an entertaining affair which would have lifted either into the top two.

Jack McGlynn scored an audacious free-kick as Stoke held off a late Blackburn comeback to win 2-1. McGlynn caught everyone off guard in the 43rd minute, finding the net with a spectacular set piece from the left instead of the expected cross to score his fourth of the campaign.

Moussa Baradji’s own goal in the 68th minute gave the Potters a deserved cushion as they seemed set for a comfortable victory. But Andri Gudjohnsen’s tap-in halved the deficit in the 87th minute and the Icelandic forward thought he had equalised three minutes later when steering a header into the far corner but referee Andrew Kitchen penalised the striker for a push, much to the fury of the Rovers fans and coaching staff. Despite the late scare, Stoke held on to make it eight wins in 11.

Norwich piled more pressure on the Derby head coach, John Eustace, after thrashing the Championship strugglers 4-0 at Pride Park. On his 47th birthday, Eustace saw his side ripped apart by the pace and movement of the Canaries, who scored three times before the break.

Anthony Musaba, Paris Maghoma and Darlin Yongwa put Norwich in complete control before substitute Jovon Makama wrapped up a third straight win for the visitors and condemned Derby to a fourth defeat in five games.

Derby have won only once this season and Friday night’s home game with Bolton now looks like a huge one for Eustace.

Sydie Peck scored a first-half hat-trick as Sheffield United edged past Preston 3-2 at Deepdale. The 22-year-old inadvertently equalised with an intended cross in the 27th minute, put his team ahead with a gorgeous second from just outside the box 10 minutes later, and sealed his treble with a tap-in on the stroke of the interval.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Leo Leroy had put the hosts in front after just two minutes and substitute Callum Lang set up a grandstand finish with a composed 77th-minute consolation. It is the first time Sheffield United have managed back-to-back wins this season but makes it just one point out of 18 for the new Preston manager, Graham Alexander.

Stephy Mavididi’s first goal for Watford earned the head coach, Alessio Dionisi, crucial breathing space with a gritty 1-0 win over toothless Lincoln at Vicarage Road.

On-loan winger Mavididi’s deflected strike less than a minute into the second half was only the Hornets’ second win in eight games and just their second clean sheet since March.

Sam Dalby’s sixth goal of the season earned Bolton a 1-0 victory at misfiring Charlton.

The result piles more pressure on the Addicks manager, Nathan Jones, with the south-east Londoners now winless in 11 matches, A fourth straight Championship loss drops them to 21st in the table.

Jonathan Varane denied Burnley a first win under their new head coach, Fabio Celestini, as QPR fought back for a 1-1 draw.

Largie Ramazani had Burnley dreaming of only their second victory of the season when he fired them ahead at Loftus Road. But Varane’s second-half strike earned Rangers a point, with a little help from the Burnley goalkeeper Grégoire Coudert.

#825. Mee and Kenny handed first Northern Ireland call-ups

Dermot Mee and Eoin Kenny are both underage internationals with Northern Ireland

Manchester United goalkeeper Dermot Mee and Portsmouth forward Eoin Kenny have been handed their first Northern Ireland call-ups for November's final Nations League matches with Ukraine and Hungary.

Mee, 23, is a former Northern Ireland underage international and, although he has not played competitively for United this season, will add competition to NI's first choice goalkeeper Pierce Charles.

"He's been on [Under-]21s in the past so he knows a lot of the players," said manager Michael O'Neill.

"He's currently third-choice at Manchester United, he's involved obviously in their Champions League squads and I had a good chat with Jonny Evans about him. He spoke very highly of him."

Attacker Kenny, who is the son of former Republic of Ireland manager Stephen, joined Portsmouth from Dundalk in July.

The 20-year-old has made one league appearance for the Championship club, but has been handed a first call after impressing for the Northern Ireland Under-21s under Tommy Wright.

"I think this is really a reward for a strong campaign for Tommy in the 21s," added O'Neill.

"He made that move from from Dundalk to Portsmouth in the summer and it just gives us a chance to see him."

Striker Dion Charles and goalkeeper Bailey Peacock-Farrell drop out of the squad.

Sunderland defender Dan Ballard is missing after he injured his hamstring in the September win over Georgia in Tbilisi, while defender Eoin Toal, midfielders Ali McCann and Jamie McDonnell are also absent through injury.

Liverpool's Conor Bradley, who has not played since January, remains a long-term absentee.

Family affair at Croke Park caps Mee's special night

Michael O'Neill's side are unbeaten at the top of League B2 and can earn promotion to the top tier for the first time.

Northern Ireland face Ukraine at Windsor Park on Saturday, 14 November at 19:45 GMT before they travel to Hungary in their final match on 17 November.

Both games are live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sounds.

The average of Northern Ireland's squad is just 23.5, and 17 of the 25 players selected are aged 23 or under.

O'Neill admitted he would rather have the likes of the injured Ballard, Bradley, McCann and Toal available, but he knows the window will be important in building depth in the squad.

"I think that the squad has to continue to develop players, they have to step in and you have to give players the opportunity to do that," he said.

"It's a very young squad and it will be stretched again. We'll be tested in these two games, but we given ourselves a good chance with obviously what we've done to date in the games."

Northern Ireland are the only side left in the entire Nations League who have yet to concede a goal in this year's competition.

Shea Charles scored a last-gasp winner in Georgia in September before a goalless draw at home to Hungary.

A 3-0 victory over Ukraine was one of the most impressive performances from O'Neill's young side, and they ended the quadruple-header with another goalless draw, this time at home to Georgia.

If Northern Ireland can top the group they would not only win promotion to League A, but they would also be all but guaranteed of a play-off for Euro 2028.

Goalkeeper: Pierce Charles (QPR - on loan from Manchester City), Conor Hazard (Wycombe Wanderers), Dermot Mee (Manchester United)

Defenders: Trai Hume (Sunderland), Tom Atcheson (Blackburn Rovers), Ciaron Brown (Oxford United), Ruairi McConville (Norwich City), Paddy McNair (Hull City), Terry Devlin (Portsmouth), Brodie Spencer (Oxford United), Michael Forbes (Dundee)

Midfielders: Shea Charles (Fulham), Ethan Galbraith (Stoke City), Kieran Morrison (Sheffield Wednesday - on loan from Liverpool), Paul Smyth (QPR), Isaac Price (West Brom), Justin Devenny (Stoke City), Jordan Thompson (Preston North End), Patrick Kelly (Barnsley)

Forwards: Jamie Donley (Luton Town - on loan from Spurs), Ceadach O'Neill (Arsenal), Eoin Kenny (Portsmouth), Josh Magennis (Stevenage), Callum Marshall (Luton Town), Braiden Graham (Everton).
